messages.author: d12379035be5c6f9
messages.subject: Abundance estimate distsamp() vs pcount()
parts:
Estimados,

I am running pcount() and distsamp() to estimate abundance. I would expect similar results. However differences between both functions are huge.

pcount() estimate: 8.25
distsam() estimate: 65.37

I wonder if survey effort has any influences on this. I know that survey effort has influences in density estimates- In pcount() survey effort is the number of visits, but this cannot be included in distsamp().

I will appreciate any information on this subject,

All the best,

Adrian

regards

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Abundance estimate distsamp() vs pcount()
parts:
Hi Andy,

This is the data set I am using in both analysis and the code I am using in unmarked. Please can you have a look on it to see if there is something wrong?

library(unmarked)
setwd("C:/Users/Usuario/Documents/WCS/Bandurria")
bandurria.data <- read.csv("bandurria4.csv", header=TRUE)
db<- c(0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250)
yDat <- formatDistData(bandurria.data, distCol="Dist", transectNameCol="Point", dist.breaks=db)
bandurria.umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=yDat, survey="point", dist.breaks=db, unitsIn="m")
Halfnorm<- distsamp(~1 ~1, bandurria.umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="kmsq")
Exp<- distsamp(~1 ~1, bandurria.umf, keyfun="exp", output="density", unitsOut="kmsq", starts=c(8, 0))
Hazard<- distsamp(~1 ~1, bandurria.umf, keyfun="hazard", output="density", unitsOut="kmsq")
Uniform<- distsamp(~1 ~1, bandurria.umf, keyfun="uniform", output="density", unitsOut="kmsq")

Results in each model are as follow:  distsamp() vs. Distance 6.2

Halfnorm 189.4603 vs. 138.159
Exp 604.0964 vs. 398.849
Hazard 648.1934 vs. 278.269
Uniform 19.69325 vs. 30.770

Best regards,

Adrian

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Abundance estimate distsamp() vs pcount()
parts:
hi Adrian,
 your analysis looks correct from what I can tell.
 I don't know enough about Distance to be able to decipher the difference, however.
 Presumably both are based on a 250m point count circle.

 The only difference should be that unmarked is using a Poisson assumption for N whereas I'm guessing Distance computes a conditional estimator of density. That should not lead to a big difference in my view.

regards
andy

parts:
Hi Adrian,

I did some testing of unmarked and DISTANCE a long time ago, and they produced almost the exact same results. However, you have to change some of the defaults in DISTANCE if you want to compare equivalent models. For example, you need to turn off the key function adjustments.

Richard
